chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Ibn Abi 'Umayr from Hammad ibn 'Uthman from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) said:

I said to him, 'I intend to perform Umrah with the right of enjoyment until Hajj; so what should I say?' He said, 'You should say: O Allah, I intend to perform Umrah with the right of enjoyment until Hajj, according to Your Book and the Sunnah of Your Prophet (SAWW). And if you wish, you can keep in mind what you intend.'

key_terms.أَضْمَرْتَ: You kept it in mind/intended silently
key_terms.أَنْ أَتَمَتَّعَ: That I enjoy/perform with the right of tamattu'
key_terms.وَسُنَّةِ نَبِيِّكَ: And the Sunnah of Your Prophet

ai.seo_question: What is the correct formula for saying when performing Umrah before Hajj?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Istibsar highlights the flexibility in the verbal declaration (talbiyah) for Umrat al-Tamattu', emphasizing that the core requirement is the intention (niyyah) rather than a rigid formula. It underscores the Shia scholarly principle that linking the act to the Quran and Sunnah provides the necessary spiritual grounding, while allowing the specific phrasing to remain internal if desired. This reflects the broader juristic view that intention is the essence of worship, with words serving as a supportive expression.
